events.title: Locke's Two Treatises of Government
events.text: John Locke's Two Treatises of Government appears anonymously in December 1689 (title page dated 1690). The Second Treatise grounds government in natural rights and a social contract, and became a foundational text of liberalism.

events.title: Paine's Common Sense
events.text: Thomas Paine publishes Common Sense in January 1776, a widely read pamphlet making the case for American independence.

events.title: Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations
events.text: Adam Smith's An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations is published in London. It has been called the first comprehensive defense of free-market policy.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.text: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence, drafted by Thomas Jefferson in June 1776, asserting unalienable rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

events.title: Spooner's American Letter Mail Company
events.text: Lysander Spooner starts the American Letter Mail Company to compete with the U.S. Post Office's monopoly, arguing Congress could create a postal service but not ban competition. Government legal action and an 1851 law put it out of business, though postage rates fell.

events.title: Thoreau's 'Resistance to Civil Government'
events.text: Henry David Thoreau, jailed in 1846 for refusing to pay his poll tax in protest of slavery and the Mexican War, publishes the essay later known as 'Civil Disobedience.'

events.title: Bastiat's The Law
events.text: French economist Frédéric Bastiat publishes La Loi (The Law) months before his death, describing a just system of law and warning against 'legal plunder.'

events.title: Mill's On Liberty
events.text: John Stuart Mill publishes On Liberty, a defense of individual freedom grounded in his utilitarian ethics.

events.title: Spooner's No Treason
events.text: Spooner publishes 'No Treason: The Constitution of No Authority,' rejecting the Constitution's authority. It remains widely cited in libertarian anarchist thought.

events.title: Benjamin Tucker launches Liberty
events.text: Benjamin Tucker begins publishing Liberty, the leading journal of American individualist anarchism, which runs until 1908.

events.title: Mises publishes Socialism
events.text: Austrian economist Ludwig von Mises publishes Socialism, a critique of central planning (English translation 1936). His treatise Human Action follows in 1949.

events.title: Hayek's The Road to Serfdom
events.text: F. A. Hayek's The Road to Serfdom is published in Britain in March 1944 and in the U.S. that September. A Reader's Digest condensation in April 1945 brought it to a mass American audience.

events.title: Leonard Read founds FEE
events.text: Leonard Read, with Henry Hazlitt, founds the Foundation for Economic Education, often called the oldest free-market think tank in the U.S. Hazlitt's Economics in One Lesson is also published in 1946.

events.title: Mont Pelerin Society founded
events.text: Hayek convenes economists and philosophers, including Mises and Milton Friedman, near Lake Geneva, where they form the Mont Pelerin Society to revive classical liberal ideas.

events.title: Ayn Rand's Atlas Shrugged
events.text: Random House publishes Ayn Rand's Atlas Shrugged. The novel drew many young readers to individualist and pro-capitalist ideas and helped grow the early libertarian movement.

events.title: Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom
events.text: Milton Friedman publishes Capitalism and Freedom, which argued for free trade, flexible exchange rates, school vouchers and private retirement accounts.

events.title: Reason magazine founded
events.text: Lanny Friedlander, a Boston University student, publishes the first issue of Reason in May 1968 as a mimeographed newsletter. It became the flagship of the Reason Foundation, founded in 1978.

events.title: Karl Hess's 'The Death of Politics' and the YAF split
events.text: Former Goldwater speechwriter Karl Hess publishes 'The Death of Politics' in Playboy (March 1969). The same year, libertarians split from Young Americans for Freedom at its convention and the Society for Individual Liberty is formed.

events.title: The Nolan Chart is published
events.text: David Nolan publishes his two-axis chart of economic and personal freedom in the January 1971 issue of The Individualist. It was later popularized as the 'World's Smallest Political Quiz.'

events.title: Libertarian Party founded
events.text: After months of meetings that began at David Nolan's home in Colorado, a small committee formally launches the Libertarian Party. Nolan served as the first national chair.

events.title: First LP ticket and Tonie Nathan's electoral vote
events.text: John Hospers and Tonie Nathan run as the first LP ticket, drawing fewer than 4,000 popular votes. Virginia elector Roger MacBride, pledged to Nixon, casts his vote for them, making Nathan the first woman to receive an electoral vote.

events.title: For a New Liberty and The Machinery of Freedom
events.text: Murray Rothbard publishes For a New Liberty: The Libertarian Manifesto and David Friedman publishes The Machinery of Freedom, two influential cases for a society without a state.

events.title: Nozick's Anarchy, State, and Utopia
events.text: Philosopher Robert Nozick publishes Anarchy, State, and Utopia, a defense of the minimal state that won the National Book Award in 1975. Hayek shares the Nobel Prize in economics the same year; Friedman wins it in 1976.

events.title: Cato Institute established
events.text: Ed Crane, with Charles Koch's funding and Murray Rothbard's help, establishes the Cato Institute in San Francisco (it grew out of the Charles Koch Foundation of 1974). It moved to Washington, D.C., in 1982.

events.title: Free to Choose airs on PBS
events.text: Milton and Rose Friedman's ten-part PBS series Free to Choose airs, alongside a companion book that became the best-selling nonfiction book of 1980.

events.title: Ed Clark's presidential campaign
events.text: LP nominee Ed Clark, with running mate David Koch, wins 921,128 votes (about 1.06%), the party's best result until 2012 by votes and 2016 by share. He took 11.7% in Alaska.

events.title: Mises Institute founded
events.text: Lew Rockwell, then chief of staff to Rep. Ron Paul, founds the Ludwig von Mises Institute in Auburn, Alabama, devoted to Austrian economics.

events.title: Ron Paul as LP presidential nominee
events.text: Former Republican Rep. Ron Paul, nominated at the 1987 convention in Seattle with Andre Marrou as running mate, appears on the ballot in 46 states and wins 431,750 votes (about 0.5%).

events.title: Institute for Justice founded
events.text: Chip Mellor and Clint Bolick found the Institute for Justice, a libertarian public-interest law firm litigating economic liberty, property rights, school choice and free speech cases.

events.title: Rothbard's paleolibertarian strategy
events.text: Murray Rothbard's essay 'Right-Wing Populism: A Strategy for the Paleo Movement' urges an alliance of libertarians and cultural conservatives aimed at 'Middle America.' He and Lew Rockwell backed Pat Buchanan in 1992; the strategy remains debated.

events.title: Free State Project announced
events.text: Jason Sorens proposes in July 2001 that 20,000 libertarians move to one low-population state. Participants chose New Hampshire in 2003, and the pledge count passed 20,000 in 2016.

events.title: Ron Paul's 'money bomb'
events.text: Supporters of Ron Paul's 2008 Republican presidential bid raise more than $4 million online in one day, then a record for a one-day internet political fundraiser.

events.title: Students For Liberty and Young Americans for Liberty
events.text: Students For Liberty forms after its first conference at Columbia University, and Young Americans for Liberty grows out of the Students for Ron Paul campaign the same year.

events.title: Ron Paul's 2012 campaign ends active primaries
events.text: Ron Paul stops spending on remaining Republican primaries and shifts to collecting delegates at state conventions. He never formally endorsed nominee Mitt Romney.

events.title: Colorado and Washington legalize cannabis
events.text: Voters pass Colorado's Amendment 64 (55.3% yes) and Washington's Initiative 502, making them the first states to legalize recreational marijuana for adults 21 and over.

events.title: Orlando convention debate
events.text: At the televised LP presidential debate in Orlando, delegates jeer Gary Johnson for supporting driver's licenses and for saying he would have voted for the Civil Rights Act of 1964. He wins the nomination the next day on the second ballot.

events.title: Johnson-Weld best LP result
events.text: Gary Johnson and Bill Weld win 4,489,221 votes (3.28%), the best result in the party's history.

events.title: Justin Amash joins the Libertarian Party
events.text: Rep. Justin Amash of Michigan, who left the Republican Party in July 2019, joins the LP in April 2020, becoming the first Libertarian member of either house of Congress. He explored but declined a presidential run.

events.title: Jo Jorgensen's campaign
events.text: LP nominee Jo Jorgensen and running mate Spike Cohen win 1,865,535 votes (1.2%).

events.title: Mises Caucus wins control in Reno
events.text: At the national convention in Reno, Mises Caucus candidate Angela McArdle is elected party chair with about 69% of delegates, and the caucus takes every national leadership post. Delegates remove the platform's abortion plank; the caucus had also sought to drop a line condemning bigotry as 'irrational and repugnant.'

events.title: Javier Milei elected in Argentina
events.text: Economist Javier Milei, widely described as a libertarian, wins Argentina's presidential runoff with 55.7% and takes office December 10, 2023.

events.title: Washington, D.C., convention
events.text: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (May 24) and Donald Trump (May 25) address the LP convention; Trump is repeatedly booed. Delegates nominate Chase Oliver on the seventh ballot, with Mike ter Maat as running mate.

events.title: Chase Oliver's result
events.text: Chase Oliver wins 0.42% of the popular vote. Four state affiliates had denounced his nomination.

events.title: Ross Ulbricht pardoned
events.text: President Trump pardons Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht, who had been serving two life sentences. Trump had promised LP convention delegates in May 2024 to commute the sentence.

events.title: New national chair after McArdle resigns
events.text: After Angela McArdle resigns as chair on January 25, 2025, national committee member Steven Nekhaila wins a special election over Mises Caucus founder Michael Heise.
